lead: A cloud data centre spends most of its electricity on servers that are switched on but mostly idle. The binding cost is power, not CPU seconds, so providers consolidate work, switch idle hosts off and place VMs where power is used best. Power is measured in watts, energy in kilowatt-hours, and PUE compares total facility power with IT power. Only a few universities teach this as a separate chapter.
prereq: You need host utilisation and consolidation from Chapter 4.4 and placement and migration decisions from Chapter 4.5.

blocks.text: A server draws power even at zero load. A common model is:

blocks.where: P is power in watts (W); P_idle is power at zero load; P_max is power at full load; u is utilisation, 0 ≤ u ≤ 1 (fraction of capacity used).

blocks.text: With P_idle = 200 W and P_max = 400 W, a server at u = 0.3 draws 200 + 200 × 0.3 = 260 W. That is more than half its peak, so idle servers waste most of the power. Energy is power over time: E = P × t, in kilowatt-hours (kWh), with P in kW and t in hours.
PUE = total facility power ÷ IT power
blocks.where: PUE (power usage effectiveness) is dimensionless; cooling, fans, UPS losses and lighting make it above 1. PUE = 1.5 means 1 kW of IT needs 1.5 kW at the meter.

sections.h3: Techniques: consolidate, sleep, slow down, site

items: Consolidation with live migration. Pack VMs onto fewer hosts, move the rest with live migration, then switch empty hosts off. This removes the idle floor.
DVFS and low-power states. Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling lowers CPU voltage and clock when load falls; sleep states cut whole hosts.
Power-aware placement. A scheduler that knows each host's power curve chooses the host that adds least watts for the same SLA, not the one with most free RAM.
Renewable-aware scheduling. Delay flexible batch jobs to hours when solar or wind supply is high, if the SLA allows.
Free cooling and climate siting. Cold climates, outside-air cooling and efficient cooling design lower PUE.

blocks.text: Use energy per transaction, energy per VM-hour and carbon per kWh (gCO₂/kWh). A low PUE and high utilisation give a low energy per VM-hour. The same ideas work in reverse: a badly chosen placement, a heavy replication factor, or keeping replicas on hot idle hosts raises the power bill. See Chapter 4.6 for replication trade-offs.

figure.caption: The line is the model P = 200 + 200u: at 30 percent load a server draws 260 W, not 120 W, because the flat 200 W idle floor never goes away. The two marked points are the worked example — 100 servers at u = 0.3, then consolidation onto 40 servers at u = 0.75 — which cuts monthly facility energy from 28,470 kWh to 15,330 kWh.

spec.aria: A straight line rises from 200 W at zero utilisation to 400 W at full load, sitting above a flat 200 W idle floor, with one point marked at 30 percent load and 260 W and another at 75 percent load and 350 W.

examples.question: A data centre has 100 servers, each P_idle = 200 W and P_max = 400 W, at 30 percent average utilisation. Cooling gives PUE = 1.5 and power costs ₹8 per kWh. Find monthly energy and cost, then the same after consolidation onto 40 servers at 75 percent. Use 730 hours per month.
steps: 3. Monthly IT energy = 26 kW × 730 h = 18,980 kWh.
examples.answer: Monthly facility energy falls from 28,470 kWh to 15,330 kWh and cost from ₹2,27,760 to ₹1,22,640, a 46.15 percent cut for the same work.

traps: Applying PUE in the wrong direction: multiply IT energy by PUE to get facility energy, never divide.
Mixing power (kW, an instant) with energy (kWh, over time); the bill is in kWh, so a missing 730 hours is a factor-of-730 error.
Using u = 30 instead of 0.30 in the power model, which gives 6,200 W instead of 260 W.
Treating power as proportional to load: a 30 percent loaded server draws 260 W here, not 120 W, because the idle floor never disappears.

quiz.q: Define PUE and give its formula.
quiz.a: PUE = total facility power ÷ IT power; dimensionless, above 1.

quiz.q: Why does a 30% loaded server with P_idle = 200 W and P_max = 400 W draw 260 W, not 120 W?
quiz.a: It draws idle power plus a load-dependent part: 200 + 200 × 0.3 = 260 W.

quiz.q: A host has P_idle = 150 W and P_max = 350 W. Find P at u = 0.4.
IT energy is 5,000 kWh and PUE = 1.4. Find facility energy.
Why can consolidation raise SLA risk, and what limits it?
quiz.a: Packing raises host utilisation, so a burst can violate the SLA; live migration and headroom limits cap the packing.

quiz.q: A scheduler picks a host with most free RAM but a poor power curve. Why may this raise cost?
quiz.a: The host may add many watts for the same work; power-aware placement should compare added watts under the SLA.

beyond: Not for the exam. Industry tools measure PUE and host power in real time and feed a power-aware scheduler; providers also publish renewable-energy matching. Research moves to carbon-aware scheduling and battery-backed workloads. Search for 'power-proportional computing', 'DVFS', and 'carbon-aware scheduling'.
